paragraphs.text:
We consider an AFDM-GFRA system, where a LEO satellite equipped
with $M=M_yM_z$ antennas serves $K$ single-antenna devices
\cite{ding2026}. During each transmission block, active devices
share the same time-frequency resources to transmit their pilots
to the satellite. Additionally, to minimize energy consumption,
we assume that these terrestrial devices operate without GNSS
capabilities and do not pre-compensate for delay and Doppler shifts
\cite{shen2025}.

The terrestrial-satellite links (TSLs) will experience fast variations due to the high mobility of
the LEO satellite. Hence, this time variation and multipath propagation
require a doubly dispersive channel model for accurate TSLs
characterization \cite{shen2025}.
Take the ground device as the stationary reference point.
The Doppler term $\nu_k$ is assumed to be common to all propagation
paths within the same TSL \cite{huang2026}.
Let $\mathbf a_k$ denote the uniform planar array (UPA) response vector
of device $k$.
Then, after compensating for the common propagation delay $\tau_c$
at the satellite receiver, the time-varying channel impulse response
from the $k$th device to the satellite can be represented as
\begin{equation}
 \mathbf h_k(t,\tau)
 =\mathbf a_k\sum_{\ell=1}^{L_k}g_{k\ell}
 e^{j2\pi\nu_k t}\delta(\tau-\tau_{k\ell}),
 \label{eq:physical-channel}
\end{equation}
where $k=1,\ldots,K$, $n_z=0,\ldots,M_z-1$,
$n_y=0,\ldots,M_y-1$, and $L_k$ is the number of physical paths.
Additionally, the notations $g_{k\ell}$ and $\nu_k$ are the complex path
gain and Doppler shift of the $\ell$th path from $k$th device to the
satellite, respectively.
$\delta(\cdot)$ denotes the Dirac delta function.
$\tau_{k\ell}=\widetilde\tau_{k\ell}-\tau_c$ represents the differential
delay for the $\ell$th path from the $k$th device to the satellite,
where $\widetilde\tau_{k\ell}$ and $\tau_c$ are denoted as propagation
delay and common delay, respectively.
The common delay corresponds to the propagation time between the
satellite and the closest point on earth within the beam coverage
\cite{shen2025}.
Let $t$ denote the time measured from the start of the transmission block.
Let $\bigl(\mu_{y,k},\mu_{z,k}\bigr)$ denote the directional cosines.
Let $\bigl(d_y,d_z\bigr)$ denote the antenna spacings.
Let $\lambda$ denote the wavelength.
Let
\begin{equation}
 [\mathbf a_k]_{n_z+M_zn_y}
 =e^{j2\pi(d_yn_y\mu_{y,k}+d_zn_z\mu_{z,k})/\lambda}.
 \label{eq:upa}
\end{equation}
Assume that the path gains, differential delays, Doppler shifts, and
angles-of-arrival remain approximately constant within a transmission
block.

After removing the CPP and applying the DAFT, let
$H_k^{(q)}\in\mathbb C^{M\times N\times N}$ denote the effective
channel of device $k$ in frame $q$, with $H_k=H_k^{(0)}$.
To better capture the LEO channel dynamics, we incorporate
fractional delay and fractional Doppler effects, and the resulting
expression for the elements of the channel tensor $H_k$ is given
as follows \cite{huang2026}:
\begin{equation}
 H_{kmrn}
 =[\mathbf a_k]_m\sum_{\ell=1}^{L_k}g_{k\ell}
 [\mathbf G(\tau_{k\ell}/T_s,\nu_k;N_{\rm CPP})]_{rn},
 \label{eq:channel}
\end{equation}
where $H_{kmrn}$ is the channel coefficient from transmitted
DAFT-domain symbol $n$ to received DAFT-domain symbol $r$ at
antenna $m$.
$\mathbf G(d,\nu;N_{\rm CPP})$ denotes the effective channel
matrix of a path with gain $1$, normalized delay $d$, and Doppler
shift $\nu$ in frame $0$.
For the $N$ samples after CPP removal, starting at sample $g$,
this matrix is given by
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 \mathbf G(d,\nu;g)=\mathbf F_{\rm A}\mathbf D_{\nu,g}\mathbf B_d,\\
 \mathbf D_{\nu,g}=\diag\{e^{j2\pi\nu T_s(g+t)}\}_{t=0}^{N-1},\\
 [\mathbf B_d]_{tn}=\varphi_n(t-d).
 \end{gathered}
 \label{eq:path-operator-system}
\end{equation}
Here, $\varphi_n$ is the transmitted waveform when the $n$th
DAFT-domain symbol equals $1$ and all other input symbols are zero,
with the CPP defined in \eqref{eq:cpp}.
Its expression and the derivation of \eqref{eq:path-operator-system}
for fractional delays, including delays exceeding $NT_s$, are given
in Appendix~\ref{app:afdm-model}.
For frame $0$, $g=N_{\rm CPP}$.
In practical propagation environments, fractional Doppler shifts
and fractional time delays can introduce significant power leakage
in the effective channel matrix of \eqref{eq:path-operator-system},
thereby weakening the sparsity of $H_k$ \cite{huang2026}.
Since we directly estimate the full AFDM effective channel tensor
$H_k$ without imposing sparsity assumptions, using only one pilot
sequence makes \eqref{eq:mmv} underdetermined, so that multiple
pilot sequences are required \cite{huang2026}.

Fortunately, $H_k$ remains approximately constant over $Q$
consecutive frames, benefited by the quasi-static property of
\eqref{eq:physical-channel} in the delay-Doppler domain
\cite{shen2025}.
This characteristic allows the proposed scheme to gather more
observations, thereby facilitating the joint design of channel
estimation and activity detection.
Furthermore, the phase rotation $e^{j2\pi\nu_kqT_{\rm frame}}$
caused by Doppler shifts accumulates across multiple frames and
will be addressed carefully in our algorithm design \cite{shen2025}.
Since $\nu_k$ is common to all paths of device $k$,
\eqref{eq:physical-channel} yields
\begin{equation}
 \begin{gathered}
 H_k^{(q)}=e^{jq\beta_k}H_k,\\
 \beta_k=\operatorname{wrap}(2\pi\nu_kT_{\rm frame}),
 \end{gathered}
 \label{eq:twc-frame-channel}
\end{equation}
where $\operatorname{wrap}(\cdot)$ maps an angle to $[-\pi,\pi)$.

Due to the sporadic access of the devices, matrix $\mathbf X$
exhibits a block-sparsity structure. Specifically, if the $k$th
device is inactive, we have $X_k=\alpha_kH_k=\mathbf 0$
\cite{cai2026}.

In this paper, we aim to simultaneously detect the active devices
and estimate the corresponding channels based on the observation
$\mathbf Y$ under a Bayesian inference framework \cite{cai2026}.
We consider $Q<KN$ in \eqref{eq:mmv}.

In this subsection, we assume that the estimates
$\widehat{\mathbf A}$ and $\widehat\sigma^2$ are known, which are
obtained from $\mathbf Y$ as described in Section~\ref{sec:frontend}.
Let $q_{\rm tr}$ denote the prior distribution of $H_k$ represented
by the channel samples used for training.
For inference, we assume independence across devices and between
each device's activity and channel. The activities follow Bernoulli
priors, while $q_{\rm tr}(H_k)$ retains the dependence among the
coefficients within $H_k$.

Exact Bayesian estimators, e.g., the MMSE estimator, are generally
intractable due to the high-dimensional integrals in the
marginalization of the joint posterior distribution
$q(\mathbf X,\{H_k\}_{k=1}^{K},\{\alpha_k\}_{k=1}^{K}\mid\mathbf Y)$.

This paper seeks to address the aforementioned challenges by
plugging in deep generative priors for efficient message calculation
\cite{cai2026}.
